rv.q: A Dark Wood is a deeply profound play that grapples with the question of how one can keep their humanity when living in a society, a broken system, that rewards violence and brutality...
The quality of acting is strong throughout with exceptional performances by Webber and Feacher as Miss Vivian and Armadillo.
"A Dark Wood" succeeds by virtue of the robust performances of the cast and through intelligent visual design choices.

Ironically, Tin Drum’s production of A Dark Wood feeds that same flaw with its unvarying tone and pacing across all three sections, despite Coble’s well-crafted dialogue and the cast’s well-calibrated performances.

Spending almost two, uninterrupted hours in a dismal, dystopian world, became very unpleasant, gloomy and heartbreaking, and Tin Drum Theatre Company’s production only left me with a depressing feeling of hopelessness.
A Dark Wood is everything I love about small Chicago blackbox theatre productions.
I found myself more entranced with the first story, and involved with the second, but by the third, wondering exactly how they were going to meet each other at the end.

cn.t: This timely dystopian drama hits close to home with its portrayal of authoritarian suppression, though critics find the story itself somewhat familiar and lackluster despite strong performances and visual design.
